content: The TAF1 protein, also referred to as the transcription initiation factor TFIID subunit 1, TFIID 250 kDa subunit (TAFII-250), or TBP-associated factor 250 kDa (p250), is a protein encoded by the TAF1 gene in humans. Function The initiation of transcription by RNA polymerase II necessitates the coordinated activities of over 70 polypeptides. The protein responsible for orchestrating these activities is the basal transcription factor TFIID. TFIID binds to the core promoter region of DNA, ensuring the proper positioning of RNA polymerase II. It also serves as a structural scaffold for the assembly of the remaining components of the transcription complex and acts as a conduit for regulatory signals. TFIID is composed of the TATA-binding protein (TBP) and a group of evolutionarily conserved proteins known as TBP-associated factors (TAFs). TAFs play multiple roles, including participation in basal transcription, functioning as coactivators, recognizing promoter sequences, and modifying general transcription factors (GTFs) to facilitate the assembly of the transcription complex and the initiation of transcription. The TAF1 gene encodes the largest subunit of TFIID. This subunit binds to core promoter sequences that encompass the transcription start site. Additionally, it interacts with activators and other transcriptional regulators, and these interactions influence the rate of transcription initiation. The TAF1 subunit contains two independent protein kinase domains located at the N-terminal and C-terminal regions. It also exhibits acetyltransferase activity and can function as a ubiquitin-activating and conjugating enzyme. Two distinct transcripts encoding different isoforms of this protein have been identified. Histones, which are proteins that package DNA, are often acetylated to open up the chromatin structure and facilitate transcription. TAF1 contains two bromodomains, each capable of binding to one of two acetyllysine residues at positions 5 and 12 in the histone H4 tail. This interaction stabilizes the TBP-TATA box complex, which is critical for transcription initiation. Two mutations in the TAF1 gene have been reported in two families with intellectual disability, although detailed clinical information regarding these cases was not provided. Interactions TAF1 has been shown to interact with the following proteins: CSNK2A1 (Casein kinase II subunit alpha), CCND1 (Cyclin D1), GTF2F1 (General transcription factor IIF subunit 1), RB1 (Retinoblastoma protein), TAF7 (another TFIID subunit), TBP (TATA-binding protein), and UBTF (Upstream binding transcription factor).
